record.context_brief: e-autoparallel submanifolds of the quantum state manifold
record.original_question: Let S(H) be the manifold of strictly positive density operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, equipped with a monotone Riemannian metric g, the flat m-connection from the natural affine embedding, and its dual e-connection. Which e-autoparallel submanifolds does S(H) admit, or equivalently, for which pairs (rho, V) does there exist an e-autoparallel submanifold through rho with tangent space V?

evidence.quote: The problem presented here is to determine the ∇(e)-autoparallel submanifolds of S or, equivalently, to find the condition for a pair (ρ, V ) of a point ρ ∈ S and a linear subspace V of the tangent space Tρ(S) to have a ∇(e)-autoparallel submanifold which contains ρ with the tangent space V .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the manifold of strictly positive (invertible) density operators on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e., self-adjoint positive-definite operators of unit trace. The tangent space $T_\rho \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ at $\rho \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ is naturally identified with the space of traceless self-adjoint operators on $\mathcal{H}$.

Equip $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ with:
(i) a monotone Riemannian metric $g$, i.e., a Riemannian metric whose induced distance is contractive under every completely positive trace-preserving map (such metrics are classified, up to normalization, by Petz's theorem via operator-monotone functions);
(ii) the m-connection $\nabla^{(m)}$, defined as the flat affine connection inherited from the natural embedding $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H}) \hookrightarrow \{A = A^* : \operatorname{tr} A = 1\}$ as an affine subspace of self-adjoint operators;
(iii) the e-connection $\nabla^{(e)}$, defined as the dual connection of $\nabla^{(m)}$ with respect to $g$, in the sense that for all vector fields $X, Y, Z$,
$$X\, g(Y,Z) = g(\nabla^{(m)}_X Y, Z) + g(Y, \nabla^{(e)}_X Z).$$

A submanifold $M \subseteq \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ is called $\nabla^{(e)}$-autoparallel if for every pair of vector fields $X, Y$ tangent to $M$, the covariant derivative $\nabla^{(e)}_X Y$ is also tangent to $M$.

Determine all $\nabla^{(e)}$-autoparallel submanifolds of $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$. Equivalently, characterize the pairs $(\rho, V)$, where $\rho \in \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ and $V$ is a linear subspace of $T_\rho \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$, for which there exists a $\nabla^{(e)}$-autoparallel submanifold of $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{H})$ passing through $\rho$ with tangent space $V$ at $\rho$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in quantum information geometry. Existing literature (notably work on autoparallelity of quantum statistical manifolds) emphasizes that, unlike the classical case, the quantum e-connection generally has non-vanishing torsion, creating obstructions to the existence of e-autoparallel submanifolds; partial results exist for specific monotone metrics (e.g., SLD, BKM), but a general characterization of admissible pairs $(\rho, V)$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Autoparallelity of Quantum Statistical Manifolds in Light of Quantum Estimation Theory
status_evidence.snippet: The e-connection has non-vanishing torsion in general, which brings various mathematical difficulties; e-autoparallel submanifolds are studied as a quantum analogue of exponential families.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of characterizing e-autoparallel submanifolds for monotone metrics is not fully resolved, with only partial results known.

status_evidence.title: Quantum States, Groups and Monotone Metric Tensors
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the family of monotone metric tensors on faithful quantum states via group-theoretic methods.
status_evidence.claim: Monotone metrics on S(H) form a rich family (Petz classification), and their dual affine connections lack a unified treatment for autoparallelity.
